findings.title: Task 8T omits renderer tests for three outcome kinds the design requires
findings.description: The design's Technical Requirements require `renderAdoptionFacts` tests for "every outcome, the state-set notice, 'none found' facts, the squadron bullet." Task 8T enumerates only brownfield (capped), adoption-in-progress, and `NOT_EVALUATED`. The `adoption-closed`, `already-planned`, and `greenfield` outcome bullets are never asserted. This matters beyond completeness: the renderer only runs when the brownfield prompt is selected, so in production those three kinds are reachable only via the `in_progress`/`declined` state bullets path — effectively never — meaning the untested branches would be exercised by no other task (Task 12 fixtures for greenfield/planned/closed assert the *absence* of the facts section, not their rendering). Add three cases to Task 8T asserting the outcome bullet text for `adoption-closed`, `already-planned`, and `greenfield`.

findings.title: Success criteria fully cross-referenced; sequencing, commits and granularity are sound
findings.description: Coverage verified item by item: all 12 functional scenarios land in Task 12 fixtures 1–13 plus Task 9T's selection table (including "no source walk" via the `measureSourceVolume` spy, guide-check-before-write via "state still ''", and the explicit-instruction path); overrides and invalid-value rejection in Task 1T and fixture 9; CLI/MCP parity in Task 13; byte-identical planned-project build in Task 15 walkthrough step 1; the squadron-bullet isolation for slice 262 in Task 8's `renderSquadronFact()`. No scope creep: every task traces to D1–D9, the Success Criteria, or AGENTS.md workflow (Task 0). Dependencies are acyclic and respected (Task 3 seeds `adoptionOutcome.ts` with the threshold before Task 7 completes it; `import type` breaks the sourceVolume↔adoptionOutcome runtime cycle; contracts.ts import-free per F005). Every implementation task is immediately followed by its test task, and commit points sit after tested states, grouped sensibly (not after every task, not only at the end). Task 6's decision to extract `INITIATIVE_PLAN_FILE_PATTERN` instead of reusing `resolveInitiativePlanPath` is a justified, documented deviation (the existing function swallows all readdir errors, which conflicts with D6's "other read errors throw"); the function's own behavior is preserved. The MCP-level `context_build` error-result path for `AdoptionError` is covered by construction — each link is tested (fixture 12 rejects, Task 10T proves the integrator rethrows, and contextTools' generic try/catch → `errorResult` already exists) — so no separate test is needed.

findings.title: Performance NFR handled per design; no load test required for this stack
findings.description: The slice restates a performance NFR (D2: detection adds under one second to a Phase 0 build). The task file explicitly addresses it and correctly omits a `tests/load/` task: D2 itself substitutes cap assertions for timing tests ("Tests assert the caps, not timings"), Task 3T asserts both caps (early exit at the threshold, `AdoptionError` at `MAX_WALK_ENTRIES`), and the only rule defining a `tests/load/` tier is `project-documents/ai-project-guide/project-guides/rules/python.md:57`, scoped to simulation/network/concurrency/environment-layer paths — I confirmed no other rule file mentions `tests/load`, so the tier does not apply to this TypeScript repo and no CI-gating task is needed.

findings.title: Design scope line mentions `hasBuildManifest` reuse that no fact consumes
findings.description: The design's Technical Scope says "The report reuses 260's `recognizeCi` and `hasBuildManifest` unchanged," but D5's authoritative fact list (source, history, docs, adrs, ruleFiles, ci) contains no build-manifest fact, and no task uses `hasBuildManifest`. The tasks correctly follow D5, so no requirement is left unmet and no task change is needed — but the scope sentence is loose and worth cleaning up if the design is revised, so a later reader doesn't conclude the tasks dropped a fact.
